chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man whose hands and feet crack while he is in the state of Ihram; may he be treated? He said: Yes, with butter and oil. And he said: When the one in Ihram complains, let him be treated with whatever is permissible for him to eat while he is in Ihram.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What treatments are permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram for skin conditions?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a pragmatic legal principle by linking topical treatment to dietary permissibility, allowing the Muhrim to use butter and oil for cracked skin without invalidating Ihram. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) in ritual law, ensuring that necessary medical care does not become a burden during the sacred state of pilgrimage.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

Heasws was asked about a man, his hands and his legs crack while he is in Ihraam. Can he apply treatment?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, with the butter and the oil’. And heasws said: ‘When the one in Ihraam complains, so let him be treated with whatever is Permissible for him, from (that what) he eats it, while he is in Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 4. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban from those who narrated to him who has said the following:

“A man once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man in whose hands and feet cracks appear while he is in the state of Ihram; if he can use medicine. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so with oil and ghee.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If one in the state of Ihram becomes ill, one must treat the illness with what is lawful for him to eat in the state of Ihram.’”
